title: OPS-23's install timing binds 'these checks'; a present-value check run after the rescue marker would settle with a rescue_exit the marker contradicts (OPS-23, OPS-45, WIR-9a)
description:
> *Filed 2026-10-22 while judging panel B (pv-7j3, pv-p3k, pv-009, pv-gpw, pv-ss4), from a full read of the set at `1bdf453`.*

On an install, does `OPS-23`'s new present-value check have to run before the `OPS-45` markers, as the missing-field checks do?

- pv-gpw added `03:1896`: "A field that is present but fails this repeated validation fails as its writer's bullet above says, on both the error and the operation view, and settles as these missing-field failures do."
- The timing rule a few lines on reads: "On an install, these checks MUST run before either `OPS-45` marker is written: its rescue marker is "**false, written before begin rescue (`PRV-15`) is dispatched**". The install settles `failed` with `disk_effect: "none"` and `rescue_exit: "none"`". It follows "These missing-field failures settle `failed`".
- `OPS-23`'s own bound for repeated validation is only "before the driver is called".

Two readings:
- **Reading A:** "these checks" is all of the repeated validation. A present-value failure comes before the markers and settles with `rescue_exit: "none"`.
- **Reading B:** "these checks" is the missing-field checks. A present-value check may run after the rescue marker is written `false` and before begin rescue is dispatched.

Under reading B, "settles as these missing-field failures do" promises `rescue_exit: "none"`. But `WIR-9a` renders `rescue_exit` from that marker ("`none` only where no rescue session was opened"; `unknown` "where it failed or the operation died before reaching it"). So two engines can send different `rescue_exit` values for the same rejected install.

Owners: `OPS-23`, `OPS-45`, `WIR-9a`.

title: PRV-47 does not say which kind a create fails with when one validation rejects a caller value and a system-written value together (PRV-47, OPS-11, WIR-9a)
description:
Found by panel r62c (readers voted 4-0 to file it as a bead), while drafting `pv-gpw` (`docs/research/panels-2026-10/r62/final-form.md`, "File with the drain PR", item 1).

One `PRV-47` validation can reject a caller-supplied value and a value this system wrote in the same create. `PRV-47` gives the caller value `invalid_request` with `retryable: false` and, since `pv-gpw`, the system-written value `internal` with `retryable` from `OPS-11`'s create row (`true`). Nothing says which kind the create fails with when both are rejected together. Both outcomes settle `failed` with no mutation and a full release, so the difference is the kind and `retryable` the caller sees.

One reader (unvoted) argued that `internal` should win, "since a caller fix cannot clear a defect". This bead records the gap; it does not decide it.

Owners: `PRV-47`, `OPS-11`, `WIR-9a`.

title: WIR-9a's field pointer does not say what a rejected combination names: trust's exclusive members, an invalid union discriminator, an array element (WIR-9a, WIR-2, WIR-20)
description:
> *Filed 2026-10-22 while judging panel B (pv-7j3, pv-p3k, pv-009, pv-gpw, pv-ss4), from a full read of the set at `1bdf453`.*

`WIR-9a`'s new `details.field` row (pv-ss4, applied to create, install, power and delete by the owner's "Wide: all four ops") orders *several rejected fields*. It does not say which pointer names a rejection of a combination of fields.

- `WIR-9a` (`13:134`): `field` is "an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the request body", and "Where one validation step rejects several fields …, the least escaped pointer, compared by unsigned UTF-16 code units".
- `WIR-20` (`13:693`): the rescue-entering install variants "additionally carry a required `trust` object**, exactly one of three, not two". The three are `{"use_provider_keys": true}`, `{"expected_host_keys": [...]}` and `{"accept_unpinned": true}`.
- `API-13` (`04:976`): "pinned keys and "accept unpinned" MUST be mutually exclusive". `RSC-4` (`06:101`): "Caller-supplied keys and the first-use-trust opt-in MUST be mutually exclusive".

Take a `rootfs_via_rescue` install whose `trust` is `{"expected_host_keys": [...], "accept_unpinned": true}`:
- one engine names the object, `/trust`;
- one treats both members as rejected and names the least, `/trust/accept_unpinned`;
- one names the member it checked second, `/trust/expected_host_keys`.

All three can cite the row.

The same holds for any closed discriminated-union body when the discriminator itself is invalid: install's `strategy`, and `WIR-35`'s `resolution`. One engine names the discriminator. Another treats the variant's own fields as unknown under `WIR-2` and names the least of those.

Nothing says whether a bad array element is named by the array (`/ssh_public_keys`) or the element (`/ssh_public_keys/1`).

Owners: `WIR-9a`, `WIR-2`, `WIR-20`.
